questions.question: A data center must run hundreds of VMs with maximum efficiency and minimal attack surface. Which hypervisor type should it deploy?
questions.explanation: Type 1 hypervisors run directly on hardware with no host OS layer, maximizing performance and reducing attack surface. Production data centers standardize on them.

questions.question: A host needs emergency maintenance but its production VMs cannot go down. Which feature moves them to another host without interruption?
questions.explanation: Live migration transfers a running VM's memory and state to a new host with no perceptible downtime, allowing the original host to be serviced safely.

questions.question: A QA engineer must repeatedly test risky software and instantly restore the test VM to a clean state after each run. Which feature enables this?
questions.explanation: Snapshots capture VM state at a point in time, so the engineer can revert to the clean state after every test run in seconds.

questions.question: A team needs identical, lightweight application environments on every developer laptop and CI server. VMs or containers: which fits better?
questions.explanation: Containers package the app and dependencies once and run identically anywhere with a shared kernel, starting in seconds. Full VMs would be far heavier for this purpose.

questions.question: A guest OS uses specially written drivers that communicate directly with the hypervisor to speed up disk and network I/O. Which virtualization approach is this?
questions.explanation: Paravirtualized drivers (like virtio or VMware Tools components) issue hypercalls instead of relying on emulated hardware, cutting I/O overhead significantly.

questions.question: An admin must run an unmodified Windows guest on a server using Intel VT-x. Which virtualization approach makes this possible without binary translation?
questions.explanation: Hardware-assisted virtualization uses CPU extensions like VT-x and AMD-V to run unmodified guests efficiently. The CPU itself handles privileged instruction trapping.

questions.question: A host is running out of RAM, so the hypervisor inflates drivers inside guests to force them to release idle pages. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Ballooning uses a guest driver to pin and surrender memory pages back to the hypervisor under memory pressure, reclaiming RAM without killing VMs.

questions.question: A developer installs VirtualBox on a Linux laptop to run a Windows VM for testing. Which hypervisor type is being used?
questions.explanation: VirtualBox runs as an application on the host OS, making it a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor, convenient for desktops but with extra overhead.

questions.question: An application is split into 50 microservices that must scale independently and deploy in seconds. Which technology fits this workload?
questions.explanation: Containers start in seconds, pack densely, and suit independently deployable microservices. Booting a VM per service would be too slow and resource-heavy.

questions.question: A security team must run untrusted, potentially malicious code with the strongest possible isolation. Containers or VMs: which should they choose?
questions.explanation: VMs run separate kernels on virtualized hardware, so escaping a VM is much harder than escaping a container, which shares the host kernel.

questions.question: An admin assigns 64 vCPUs across VMs on a host that has only 16 physical cores, expecting the VMs will not peak simultaneously. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Overcommitment allocates more virtual resources than physically exist, banking on staggered usage. A 4:1 vCPU ratio is common, but contention degrades performance if many VMs peak together.

questions.question: A powered-off VM's files are moved to a different host and datastore over a weekend. What type of migration is this?
questions.explanation: Cold migration moves a shut-down VM, so it incurs downtime but works even without shared storage or live-migration infrastructure between hosts.

questions.question: An operations team needs a golden master image from which dozens of identical servers can be deployed rapidly. What should they create?
questions.explanation: A template is a protected master VM cloned for each new deployment, guaranteeing consistent configuration and drastically cutting provisioning time.

questions.question: A database VM's 100 GB disk must occupy its full capacity immediately on the datastore to guarantee performance and space. Which provisioning method is required?
questions.explanation: Thick provisioning allocates all disk space upfront, preventing the datastore from being overcommitted. Thin provisioning would save space but risk running out later.

questions.question: A student runs a hypervisor inside a VM to build a home lab with virtual machines inside virtual machines. What is this setup called?
questions.explanation: Nested virtualization exposes the host's hardware virtualization extensions to a guest so it can act as a hypervisor itself, commonly used for labs and training.
